data.name: Nāmakanipaio
data.description: Nāmakanipaio Campground is located 31.5 miles south of Hilo on Highway-11 at 4,000' elevation. It is a large, open grassy area with tall eucalyptus and 'ōhi'a trees. This campground has restrooms, water, picnic tables and barbecue pits. Campfires are permitted in the barbeque pits only. If there are more than 2 people in your party, you can expand to 4 people per site with another tent. Maximum stay is 7 days.
data.audioDescription: A campground in an open grassy area with grills and spots for tents. Adjacent to the camping area is a wooden building with restrooms, and beyond it a group of wooden camper cabins.
data.reservationInfo: Campgrounds are first come, first served. No reservations. Nāmakanipaio Campground is operated by Hawai'i Volcanoes Lodge Company. Please visit http://www.hawaiivolcanohouse.com or call (844)-569-8849 for more information.
data.regulationsOverview: Fires allowed in fire pits only.

fees.description: There is a self pay station at the campground. Park entrance fees also apply which are paid at the park entrance station or the after hours self pay station on the Kīlauea Visitor Center lanai.
fees.title: Per tent site

data.directionsOverview: The campground is located 31.5 miles south of Hilo on Highway 11.

data.weatherOverview: Weather may be cool and damp year-round. Daytime temperature range: 60s to 70s F. Nightime temperature range: 30s to low 50s F. We suggest that you use a tent with a good rainfly and bring warm clothing for cool days and evenings.

accessibility.wheelchairAccess: The park circle drive is asphalt and accessible
accessibility.fireStovePolicy: Fires allowed in fire pits only. Camp stoves allowed. Collecting fallen or dead wood is permitted within 100 yards (91 meters) of campground. Please note there are occasional fire bans.
accessibility.additionalInfo: Firewood may be purchased at Volcano House.

data.name: Kulanaokuaiki
data.description: Kulanaokuaiki is located off Hilina Pali Road at 3,200 feet (975 m), there are nine walk-in campsites with picnic tables. There is an accessible vault toilet; however, no water is available and campfires are not permitted. Use fueled camping stoves only. This campground is subject to closure when the area is dry and during times of high fire risk. No dogs or pets are allowed at this campground to protect endangered nene.
data.audioDescription: An open, sprawling primitive campground on a lava field with sparse vegetation and small trees.
data.reservationInfo: No reservations are taken. First come first served. Fees may be paid at the campground's self-registration station.
data.regulationsOverview: Food must be stored in a vehicle or secure container. Feeding of wildlife is prohibited. Do not leave trash or food unattended. Attaching items to trees and shrubs with nails, wire, or chains are prohibited. Alterations (digging or leveling of the ground) are prohibited. Campfires, pets (except leashed service animals), driving off road, and operating Unmanned Aerial Systems (Drones) are prohibited. Leaving camping equipment or refuse after departing is prohibited.

fees.description: There is a self pay station at the campground
fees.title: Per site

data.directionsOverview: From Kilauea Visitor Center, turn left on Crater Rim Drive for 3.3 miles (5.3km) to the intersection of Crater Rim Drive and Chain of Craters Road. Turn left on Chain of Craters Road for 2.3 miles (3.7km). Turn right on Hilina Pali Road for 4 miles (6.4km) to the campground.
